lines.source: Illustrative collaborative-AI scenario; survey Sec. IV-B
lines.text: Five organisations train one AI model together. Who actually made it better, and who should get paid?

lines.source: Illustrative generalisation example, not a measured result from the survey
lines.text: An update can fit its own data and still make the shared model worse. Test it on separate data.

lines.source: Survey Sec. II-A and IV-A; ledger integrity is distinct from contribution quality
lines.text: A blockchain can make recorded transactions harder to rewrite. But a permanent record does not tell you whether an update helped.

lines.source: Survey Sec. IV-B.1; privacy qualification is a general limitation of parameter sharing
lines.text: In federated learning, raw data can stay with each organisation. Updates travel instead. Those updates still need privacy protection.

lines.source: Survey Sec. IV-C.2, Proof of Learning ML competition, not all blockchains
lines.text: Some researchers go further: let training replace hash puzzles. The best model earns the next block. That is one design, not how every blockchain works.

lines.source: Survey Sec. II-B and V; distinguish performance evaluation from proof of computation
lines.text: A useful model and a verified training run are different claims. A good score alone does not prove how the model was trained.

lines.source: Survey Sec. IV-B.2, SUM prediction-market balance equation
lines.text: Loss measures prediction error. Compare it before and after an update on the same test data. Lower loss raises the balance. Higher loss lowers it.

lines.source: Survey Sec. IV-B.2, separate SUM Deposit Refund Take mechanism, waiting period and partial penalty
lines.text: Another rule uses a deposit. After a waiting period, agreement with the model permits a refund. Disagreement can cost part of the deposit.

lines.source: Survey Sec. IV-B.3, DeepChain Corda and MNIST prototype, reported directions only
lines.text: In the DeepChain prototype, more parties improved accuracy. More gradients reduced throughput, and more parties increased training time. Better AI can still mean a slower system.

lines.source: Author design perspective grounded in survey Sec. V; proposed use, not a deployment claim
lines.text: For organisations learning together, ask three questions: who evaluates the updates, what stays private, and is the improvement worth the cost?

lines.source: Author research perspective, not an experimental result
lines.text: Before you decide who gets paid, define what better AI means.
